newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 12.

text.p: Judge frees farmer who killed intruder: A Northland man charged with murder for shooting an intruder at his farmhouse walked free from the High Court at Auckland on Wednesday after Justice Sian Elias ruled that no jury could reasonably convict him. Page 1.
'Palace' for MPs can be stopped: It was not too late to stop plans for a new $94 million ministerial building, Parliamentary Service general manager John O'Sullivan said on Wednesday. Page 1.

Henare avoids TV interview: NZ First deputy leader Tau Henare did not appear for a promised television interview on Wednesday night because he failed to obtain a written assurance that there would be no questions about his brother-in-law, Te Tai Hauauru MP Tukoroirangi Morgan. Page 2.
DB Group interim profit improves to $17.2m: Brewer DB Group report on Wednesday a 7.5 percent rise in its tax-paid profit to $17.2 million for the six months ended March 31. Page 15.

Skellerup bonds offer brings flood of faxes: Australian securities trader Rob Ross had to close off an offer to Skellerup bondholders only hours after making it because he was swamped with faxes from potential sellers in New Zealand. Page 15.

Caltex plans to compete with dairies: New Zealand's smallest petrol company Caltex is gearing up almost a third of its 340 outlets into 24-hour a day convenience stores, with an expanded range of products to rival traditional dairies. Page 15.

Guardian Assurance reports record growth: British-owned Guardian Assurance has reported a record year in 1996 for growth in total premium income, funds under management and new premium business. Page 15.

New rules mean heads can roll: Tough code heeds painful Cave Creek lessons: Life is getting tougher for government department heads -- they can now be sacked even where no personal blame or liability can be established.
Smelter firm eyes works: A $2 million study is underway to determine the feasibility of establishing a nickel smelter in the former Ocean Beach freezing works in Southland.

Govt input wanted to prevent phone rows: The Telecommunications Users Association (TVANZ) wants the coalition government to act on the telecommunication policy document it prepared before the election and beef up the Commerce Act to support it.
Radio Otago's profits slide: A tough trading environment for radio has produced a sharply reduced profit in the March year for listed operator Radio Otago.

'Blow up Beehive': "Blow it up" is Wellington businessman Sir Robert Jones's advice to the government about the Beehive. Instead of the proposed new $94 million ministerial building the original design for Parliament House should be resurrected -- with a new wing on the vacant Beehive site, Sir Robert said. Page 1.

Fletcher's get sole MDF rights: Fletcher Wood Panels obtained exclusive rights to sell in New Zealand the medium-density fibreboard made at Rayonier New Zealand's new factory in Mataura, Southland. Page 32.

No easing on conditions -- Bancorp: The Reserve Bank is unlikely to ease monetary conditions and lower interest rates in its next statement on June 27, says the merchant bank, Bancorp, in its bulletin, "Treasury Trends". Page 32.
